evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: A00906-001; explanation and cited Jiyun entry
evidence.text: The dictionary classifies 她 as a variant of 姐. It cites the Jiyun, which lists 姐, 她, and 媎 together and says 姐’s old form included another graph, with 她 and 媎 as alternatives. It gives historical jiě and the later pronoun reading tā. This supports the historical 她–姐 spelling relation; it does not say that 也 is a phonetic component of modern 她.
evidence.title: [A00906-001] 她 (姐) - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.source: 說文解字「姐」, Shuowen.org transcription with Duan Yucai commentary
evidence.field: 姐 entry; graphic analysis and regional sense
evidence.text: The entry describes 姐 as a word for mother in Shu and 社 as the Huainan form, and analyzes 姐 as 女 plus phonetic 且. Duan Yucai comments that 社 and 姐 are close in sound. The entry supports the reported mother sense and the construction of 姐; it does not establish 也 as a component of 姐 or 她.
evidence.title: 說文解字「姐」

evidence.source: 中国作家网, article by Zhang Baoming
evidence.field: historical discussion of 她; modern reuse and dated proposal
evidence.text: The article reports that 她 appears in traditional dictionaries as an old form or variant of 姐, associated with a mother sense, and that Zhou Zuoren’s 1918-08-15 preface records Liu Bannong’s proposal to use 她 alongside 他. It describes modern 她 as reuse of an old graph with a new feminine pronoun meaning, not a demonstrated semantic continuation from the mother term. Its discussion links the proposal to both translation difficulties and contemporary social debates; it does not settle a single cause.
evidence.title: “她”自何处来

Opened the first three relevant pages; the inspected evidence supports the historical 她–姐 relation and the 1918 proposal, but not a sound-component role for 也 in 她.

search_audit.outcome: Unicode per-character pages and the exact ACC-s09381 page/image returned internal errors. The 也 and 女 Commons pages opened; their descriptions identify modern vector redraws and document stated licensing. No ancient 她 image was established.

gaps: The 也 phonetic analysis in the supplied reports is associated with an alternative old spelling of 姐, not independently established as a sound component of 她. The inspected Ministry of Education entry identifies 她 as a historical variant of 姐 but does not assign 也 a sound role.

The exact earliest written witness of 她 and the regional distribution of its historical use remain unresolved. The Ministry of Education page lists source images for 玉篇 and 集韻, but no early 她 artifact or manuscript was inspected in this pass.

The 1924 report that an education group assigned 她 the reading yi was not independently verified in this pass. The inspected sources establish the 1918 proposal and describe modern reuse; present-day tā is supported only by the supplied local row because the official Unicode record was inaccessible.

The modern Mandarin rows supplied locally are 她 tā and 也 yě; the supplied Baxter–Sagart data has 也 MC yaeX, OC *lAjʔ and no 她 row. A same-system historical comparison for the host is unavailable, and modern readings alone do not demonstrate ancient phonetic compatibility.
The exact ACC-s09381 vector lead could not be inspected. The other inspected Commons illustrations are modern redraws of individual component characters, not historical 她 forms.
